title: Financial objectives
log: 2026-10-29T12:22:32Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: No point in the bank covers financial objectives such as profitability, growth, efficiency, liquidity and solvency and how they conflict, so this needs a new point.

draft.title: Financial objectives
card: earning more revenue than expenses, so the business makes a profit. It is often shown as a profit margin or a return on investment.
Growth is an increase in the size of the business, such as higher sales or more assets. Efficiency is using resources well, so costs are kept low for the output produced.
Liquidity is the ability to pay short-term debts as they fall due, using current assets. Solvency is the ability to pay all debts, including long-term ones, and stay in business.
These objectives can conflict. For example, spending heavily on growth can use up the cash needed to pay bills on time.
draft.remember: A business sets several financial objectives, and chasing one can put another at risk.

a.q: Which objective is about a business being able to pay its short-term debts as they fall due?
a.why: Liquidity is about meeting debts that fall due soon, using current assets. Solvency is the tempting wrong answer, because it covers the ability to pay all debts, including long-term ones.
a.clue: Think about bills due soon, paid from current assets.

b.q: Kiri's bakery in Orange borrows heavily to open five new shops. Sales rise fast, but she struggles to pay suppliers each month. Which conflict does this show?
b.why: The new shops serve the growth objective, but the borrowing and spending leave too little cash for monthly bills, which is a liquidity problem. Solvency is tempting, but the problem here is paying short-term bills, not long-term debts.
b.clue: Which objective is about paying suppliers this month?
